question: What do the different columns in the stock moves history report show, like the reference and status fields?
answer: The Moves History report columns show: Date (calendar date and time of the stock move), Reference (description of the reason for the stock move or quantity change, such as a receipt number like WH/IN/00012), Product (name of the product involved in the move), Lot/Serial Number (the lot or serial number of the tracked product being moved), From (source location of the moved product), To (destination location of the moved product), Quantity (number of products moved), Unit (unit of measure of the products moved), and Status (indicates the move status, which can be Done, quantities to complete the operation) [1].
reason: The answer lists all the reference columns with matching descriptions, including Reference and Status, and adds no contradicting details.

question: How can I make Odoo pick the smallest number of packages when fulfilling an order for a product?
answer: Enable the Packages feature, then set the product category's Force Removal Strategy to Least Packages. With this strategy, Odoo fulfills an order by opening the fewest number of packages. For example, if a 100 kg package has been depleted to 54 kg, an order for 14 kg picks from that opened package, while an order exceeding 54 kg uses an unopened 100 kg package. On a delivery order, the Quantity field shows the amount automatically picked according to the removal strategy, and you can select the bulleted list icon to open the Open: Stock move pop-up, where the Pick from field shows where the quantities were picked.
reason: The answer correctly states the key steps (enable Packages, set Force Removal Strategy to Least Packages) and adds consistent detail without contradicting the reference.

question: What do the international trade terms like EXW or CIF mean, and which ones are available in Odoo?
answer: Incoterms (International Commercial Terms) are standardized trade terms used in international transactions to define the rights and responsibilities of buyers and sellers, establishing obligations related to delivery of goods, transfer of risks, and distribution of costs between the parties [1]. They specify details such as the point at which risk and costs transfer from seller to buyer, and responsibility for transportation, insurance, customs clearance, and other aspects of the transaction [1]. By default, all 11 Incoterms are available in Odoo: EXW (Ex works), FCA (Free carrier), FAS (Free alongside ship), FOB (Free on board), CFR (Cost and freight), CIF (Cost, insurance and freight), CPT (Carriage paid to), CIP (Carriage and insurance paid to), DPU (Delivered at place unloaded), DAP (Delivered at place), and DDP (Delivered duty paid) [1].
reason: The answer defines Incoterms and lists all 11 available in Odoo, matching the reference.

If your warehouses are located in more than one region, you can define the region code at the level of each warehouse instead: go to Inventory > Configuration > Warehouses, select a warehouse, set its Intrastat region, and then Save [1].

question: How do I set up a new direct debit mandate for a customer so I can collect payments from them?
answer: In the Accounting app, go to Customers > Direct Debit Mandates and click New. Fill out the Customer (the customer whose payments will be managed by this mandate), the IBAN (the customer's account to collect payments from), the SDD Scheme (CORE for B2C customers, B2B for B2B customers), and optionally an End Date after which the mandate closes automatically (if left empty, the mandate remains active until closed or revoked). Note that a valid IBAN must be defined in the bank journal used to receive SDD payments for the mandate, and the B2B scheme is optional and may not be accepted by some banks or businesses. Then click Send & Print to generate a PDF of the mandate form and send it to the customer for signature, and click Validate to activate the mandate. To print the mandate form after validation, click the gear icon and select Mandate form. [1]
reason: The answer includes all key steps from the reference (navigation, fields, Send & Print, Validate) and adds consistent extra detail without contradicting it.

question: How do I scrap a product while I'm processing a receipt or delivery order in Odoo?
answer: To scrap a product during an operation, navigate to the Inventory app. From the Inventory Overview, click the # To Process button on an operation's task card (i.e. the Receipts task card). Then, select an operation to process from the resulting list of existing orders, which opens that operation's form. Click the cog icon and select Scrap from the drop-down menu to open a Scrap Products pop-up window. In the pop-up, select the products to scrap from the Product drop-down, adjust the Quantity if necessary, and if the product is tracked by lot or serial number, specify the tracking number in the Lot/Serial field. The Source Location and Scrap Location can be changed if needed, and if a replenishment rule is set up and the product should be replenished, tick the Replenish Quantities checkbox. Once ready, click Scrap Products; a Scraps smart button appears at the top of the operation form, and clicking it shows the details of all scrap orders created from that operation. [1]
reason: The answer includes all key steps from the reference (To Process button, opening the operation, cog icon > Scrap, selecting product, adjusting quantity, Lot/Serial if tracked, clicking Scrap Products, and the Scraps smart button) with only additional correct detail.

question: How do I move last year's profits into an equity account and then lock the books so nobody can change them?
answer: To allocate the current year's earnings, create a new miscellaneous entry with a date set to the end of the fiscal year to book them to any equity account [1]. Then verify that the current year's earnings on the balance sheet correctly show a zero balance [1]. If so, a Hard Lock date can be set to the last day of the fiscal year in Accounting > Accounting > Lock Dates [1]. Note that the Hard Lock date field is irreversible and cannot be changed or overridden regardless of access rights, so it should only be set once confirmed correct [1]. Alternatively, setting a Lock Everything date to the last day (inclusive) of the preceding fiscal year is good practice; to do so, go to Accounting > Accounting > Lock Dates, and in the Lock Journal Entries window set the Lock Everything date and Save [2][3].
reason: The answer includes all key steps from the reference (miscellaneous entry at fiscal year end to equity account, verify zero current year earnings, set Hard Lock date under Accounting > Accounting > Lock Dates, and irreversibility warning), with only harmless extra detail.

question: How do I set up a withholding tax in Odoo so I can apply it on customer invoices?
answer: To set up a withholding tax in Odoo, create a negative tax by going to Accounting > Configuration > Taxes and entering a negative amount in the Amount field. Then go to the Advanced Options tab and create a retention Tax Group. If the retention is a percentage of a regular tax, create a Tax with the retention one in the Definition tab. Once created, the retention tax can be used on customer forms, sales orders, and customer invoices, and several taxes can be applied on a single customer invoice line.

question: How does Odoo handle electronic invoicing for Guatemalan tax requirements?
answer: Odoo Invoicing supports Guatemala's FEL (Factura Electrónica en Línea) e-invoicing system with native integration and automation [1][2]. It supports most mandatory FEL document types in SAT-compliant XML, including invoices (FACT), credit notes (NCRE), and debit notes (NDEB); each document is automatically submitted to a certified certifier (Infile), digitally signed, and validated by the SAT in real time [1]. All electronic documents must be issued through a certified certifier and validated by the SAT before delivery to the customer, after which the document receives a certification date and unique UUID [2]. Odoo provides centralized and secure storage of certified documents, including their XML and PDF graphical representations, with full access for audits and control processes [1]. It also automates VAT (IVA) and applicable tax computations, ensuring compliance with local tax rates, exemption rules, and reporting structures as defined by the SAT [1].
reason: The answer covers FEL integration, certified certifier submission, SAT validation, digital signature, XML format, certification date, and UUID, matching the reference's key facts.

question: How do I set up my products so that they get picked based on how close they are to expiring, and where do I configure the days for that?
answer: To pick products based on how close they are to expiring, use the FEFO (First Expired, First Out) removal strategy, which targets products for removal based on their assigned removal dates [2]. First, enable the Lots & Serial Numbers and Expiration Dates features in Inventory app > Configuration > Settings [2]. Then, on the product form's Inventory tab, under the Traceability section, set the Tracking field to either By Lots or By Unique Serial Number and select the Expiration Date option, which makes the Removal Date field (and other date fields) appear [2]. The removal date is calculated by taking the expiration date (receipt date plus the number of days in the Expiration Date field) and subtracting the number of days specified in the Removal Date field of the product form [2]. For example, with an Expiration Date of 30 days after receipt and a Removal Date of 15 days before expiration, Eggs received January 1st expire January 31st and have a removal date of January 16th [2]. Removal strategies can also be set on Product Categories [3].
reason: The answer covers enabling the features, setting tracking and expiration date, and explains the expiration/removal date day calculations, matching the reference.

question: How can I set up a product so that Odoo only orders or produces it after a customer actually places an order, instead of keeping stock on hand?
answer: Use the Replenish on Order (MTO) route, which triggers procurement or production only after a sales order is confirmed rather than keeping stock on hand [1][2]. To configure a product: go to Inventory app > Products > Products, select an existing product or click New [3]. On the product page, open the Inventory tab and enable the Replenish on Order (MTO) route in the Routes section, along with the Buy or Manufacture route [3]. The MTO route does not work unless another route is selected as well, because Odoo needs to know how to replenish the product (buy or manufacture it) [3]. If the product is purchased from a vendor, enable the Can be Purchased checkbox under the product name, then in the Purchase tab specify a Vendor and the Price; specifying a vendor is essential because Odoo cannot generate an order without knowing who the product is purchased from [3]. If the product is manufactured, make sure it has a bill of materials (BOM) configured via the Bill of Materials smart button [3].
reason: The answer correctly identifies the Make to Order (Replenish on Order) route and explains the configuration steps, matching the reference's key facts.

question: How do I turn on multiple currencies in my accounting and set up automatic exchange rate updates?
answer: To turn on multiple currencies, go to Accounting > Configuration > Settings > Currencies and tick Multi-Currencies. Under 'Post Exchange difference entries in:', provide a Journal, a Gain Account, and a Loss Account, then click Save [1]. Once multi-currency is enabled, all currencies are created by default but not necessarily active; to activate new currencies, click 'Activate Other Currencies' under the Multi-Currencies setting or go to Accounting > Configuration > Accounting: Currencies [1]. To set up automatic exchange rate updates, go back to Accounting > Configuration > Settings > Currencies, check Automatic Currency Rates, set the Interval to your desired frequency (Daily, Weekly, or Monthly instead of Manually), optionally choose the Service to obtain rates from, and click Save [1][2]. You can also click the Update now button (🗘) beside the Next Run field to update rates manually [1].
reason: The answer matches the reference by covering enabling Multi-Currencies, setting Journal/Gain/Loss accounts, activating currencies, configuring Automatic Currency Rates with Interval and Service, and using Update now.

question: How can I make sure the oldest stock gets picked first when fulfilling orders, so older items don't sit around too long?

question: How can I make Odoo pick products with the closest expiration date first when fulfilling orders?

question: How do I make Odoo reserve whatever stock is available for an order instead of only reserving complete packages?
